prior.note: tests/onlineCoordinator.test.ts drives the real owner's linkStats (src/main/network/onlineSession.ts:L579-583). It checks that a fresh figure is returned, that the figure is null after 5001 ms (fake Date, and the clock is Date.now()-based), and that it is null for an attemptId not in peers.ready(). It also sends a retired controller's stats for the new, ready attempt and expects null. Without the transport guard that case would return {lan,5}, so the test fails for the right reason.

scripts/network/duel-app-smoke.ts:L167-168 refuses the recursive delete unless resolve(reportPath,'..') starts with resolve('out')+sep. `sep` is imported at L16. A refused path sets `failure`, and that fails the run at L186.

In src/network/rtc/peer.ts sampleStats sets route/rtt to null before scanning and assigns them only with a pair. The catch also nulls them. The rtcPeer test covers the sequence pair, then no pair, then pair again, then a throwing getStats.

In onlineDuel.ts a null poll answer clears rttMs and keeps route (Decision 4). frame() calls overlay?.draw(null) on both early returns. The session test checks 'RTT 40 MS', then 'RTT - MS' with the INTERNET label kept, which matches the format at latencyOverlay.ts:L20. It then checks a null draw when there is no state.

groupRooms counts a dropped record only when the kept record is a different one with a different startedAtIso, so the same record read twice is not counted. formatReport adds the warning to the header line. The test covers 2 duplicates, the re-read case and the clean case.

soloRecorder.ts takes over duelMode's previous logic unchanged: rising-edge count, then reset of the count and startedAtIso on each record. duelMode.ts wires framePaused after runtime.frame and passes record() into onRound. The test covers two user pauses with a blur in between giving 2, the next round's start time taken from the previous record, and a pause held across a record not counting as a new edge.
